title: Rapido's Ownly Brings Zero-Commission Food Delivery to Hyderabad
excerpt: Hyderabad is Ownly's second city after Bengaluru. Restaurants pay no commission, customers pay food plus delivery, and Rapido's Captains carry the orders — launched with a biryani party for the riders.
body:
• Rapido has launched Ownly, its standalone food-delivery app, in Hyderabad — its second city after Bengaluru, where it piloted in March.
  • Ownly charges restaurants zero commission; customers pay for the food plus a delivery fee, with no platform fee on top.
  • Hyderabad starts with about 10,000 restaurants, with a target of 30,000; in Bengaluru, Ownly says it has crossed 50,000 orders a day at an average order value near Rs. 250.
  • Deliveries are handled by Rapido Captains, the company's existing bike-taxi riders, giving them a second income stream.

Rapido has launched Ownly, its standalone food-delivery platform, in Hyderabad, making the city the second market for an app that is trying to undercut Swiggy and Zomato on how a food order is priced. Ownly began as a pilot in Bengaluru in March and went citywide there before the Hyderabad expansion, according to Restaurant India and Agro & Food Processing.

A different bill

Ownly's pitch is structural. Restaurants pay no commission on orders. Customers pay for the food and a delivery fee that the company says reflects the actual cost of the delivery, with no additional platform charges. That contrasts with the commission-plus-fees model of the established aggregators, where restaurant commissions and customer-side platform and packaging fees both sit between the menu price and the final bill.

The company says the average order value on Ownly is around Rs. 250, against roughly Rs. 400-420 on Swiggy and Zomato — a gap it attributes to lower-priced everyday orders rather than discounting. Co-founder Aravind Sanka has said delivery accounts for about 85-90 per cent of the cost of running a food-delivery business for existing aggregators, which is why Ownly is built on Rapido's existing technology, operations teams and logistics network instead of a separate fleet.

"Hyderabad is one of the most passionate food cities in the country, especially when it comes to biryani; and that makes it a natural next home for Ownly. Our model is simple: restaurants keep what they earn, customers pay only for their food and delivery, and nobody pays for anything in between."

— Aravind Sanka, Co-Founder of Rapido and Ownly

Captains, biryani and the launch

Deliveries in Hyderabad will be made by Rapido Captains, the riders who already run the company's bike-taxi and mobility network, taking food orders alongside ride requests. The company says that gives Captains an additional earning opportunity as order volumes grow, rather than requiring a new delivery workforce.

To mark the launch, Ownly hosted a biryani party for Captains from across Hyderabad — a deliberate choice in a city whose best-known dish is biryani — with Telugu actor Nani joining the event and spending time with the Captain community. The celebration was the colour around the launch, not the substance: the commercial bet is the zero-commission model and the shared fleet.

How big is the challenge?

Hyderabad starts with about 10,000 restaurants on the platform, with Ownly aiming to reach 30,000. In Bengaluru, the company says it crossed 50,000 orders a day about five months after its citywide launch, which Moneycontrol estimates at roughly 10 per cent of the city's food-delivery market, up from about 7 per cent in July. About 15 per cent of its new Bengaluru orders, the company says, come from people ordering food online for the first time.

The scale gap remains large. Zomato processes more than 2.5 million food orders a day nationally and Swiggy around 2-2.2 million. Ownly has said it plans to expand to Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Surat in the next quarter. Whether a zero-commission model stays viable as volumes rise — and whether restaurants pass any of the saving into menu prices — is the test Hyderabad will help answer. For Hyderabad diners, the practical step is simple: compare the final bill for the same order on Ownly against the app you already use, delivery fee included.
